automation.name: XQueue Scheduled Publisher
automation.description: Bounded, fail-closed scheduled publisher that selects and publishes eligible XQueue content according to explicit production policy.

goal.outcome: Publish eligible XQueue content to the intended X account according to production schedule and content policy.
goal.success_condition: Each eligible work item is published at most once, at an allowed time, under the intended production authority, with execution state and remote outcome recorded truthfully.
goal.correct_non_execution: Publish nothing when no item is due, production authority is absent, prerequisites fail, state is ambiguous, backlog requires disposition, identity is wrong, concurrency authority cannot be established, or another production gate fails.

trigger.description: Production scheduler periodically invokes XQueue eligibility and publication processing.
trigger.cadence_or_condition: The production authority configuration pins a 15-minute scheduler cadence. Whether that authority is currently deployed and active must be established from runtime or deployment evidence rather than inferred from repository configuration.

source_of_truth.description: Authored content and explicit production scheduling policy.

work_item.definition: One uniquely identified queued XQueue content item eligible for publication.
work_item.selection_rule: Select only work that is eligible under schedule policy, publication ledger state, runtime health, and production authority.

risk.rationale: The automation performs public external side effects on a production social account and duplicate or incorrect execution may be publicly visible and difficult to fully reverse.
risk.worst_credible_effect: Unauthorized, duplicate, incorrectly timed, or policy-invalid public publication from the production account.

authority.executor: XQueue production publisher running in the Cloudflare Worker runtime.
authority.production_authority: Explicit production scheduler authority configuration must be active before live publication is permitted.
authority.coordination_mechanism: Publication authority and D1-backed publication lease/fencing prevent concurrent scheduled executions from independently owning the same production publication operation.
authority.revocation_mechanism: Disable or remove production scheduler/publication authority configuration so scheduled invocations cannot perform live publication.

policy.description: Defines allowed schedule behavior, content constraints, deferrals, validation, and publication eligibility.

side_effects.operation: Create a public X post, potentially including referenced media.
side_effects.idempotency_strategy: Persist execution intent before the external create operation, maintain durable publication state, prevent concurrent ownership, and block blind retry when the remote result is ambiguous until reconciliation occurs.
side_effects.maximum_scope: At most one eligible publication per execution.

state.ledger: Production durable publication ledger; Cloudflare production state is persisted in D1 and the local publisher retains its local durable state model where applicable.
state.write_safety: State transitions must be durable and protected against concurrent publication ownership; local state writes are atomic and Cloudflare production execution uses persisted transactional state and publication fencing.

ambiguity.detection: A create request may have escaped to the remote provider without a conclusive provider result being received locally.
ambiguity.on_unknown: Record the operation as requiring reconciliation and block later automatic live publication that could create a duplicate.
ambiguity.reconciliation: The owner verifies the actual production X account and records whether the attempted item was posted or positively verified as not posted before normal publication resumes.

dispatch.strategy: Do not retry the external create operation within the same dispatch attempt. A conclusively non-executed work item may only be reconsidered by a later scheduler invocation under the scheduler_reevaluation policy.
dispatch.backoff: No in-dispatch retry loop is permitted for the public create operation.

scheduler_reevaluation.condition: A later scheduler invocation may reevaluate the work item only when durable state and remote truth establish that the prior attempt is conclusively safe to reconsider under current eligibility policy.

backlog.stale_definition: Unresolved work outside the runtime grace window is stale and must not be silently flushed as normal catch-up work.

verification.preflight: pnpm verify and the applicable production preflight/readiness gates must pass before changing or granting production authority.
verification.dry_run: pnpm post:dry and non-mutating readiness/simulation paths are used before live publication where applicable.
verification.postcondition: The selected work item, durable publication state, and actual remote X outcome must agree after a live operation.
verification.runtime_health: Runtime health and scheduled execution telemetry must show valid authority, healthy state, no unresolved reconciliation blocker, and safe eligibility before mutation.
verification.evidence: Repository tests, docs/evidence artifacts, production runtime logs, Cloudflare invocation telemetry, and provider-side publication identifiers where applicable.

recovery.procedure: Follow docs/RUNBOOK.md. Preserve durable state, classify the failure, reconcile ambiguous remote outcomes, disposition stale work explicitly, re-run health/preflight gates, and only then restore production authority.
fail_closed_conditions: Unresolved stale backlog requiring owner disposition
Unable to prove intended account identity
Unable to establish publication concurrency ownership
recovery.resume_gate: Production execution resumes only after the blocking condition is resolved and the applicable runtime-health and preflight gates pass.

owner_reserved_actions: Approve or change stale backlog disposition
Grant, transfer, or revoke production scheduler authority
Override or change production safety policy

observability.logs: Cloudflare Worker invocation logs and applicable local publisher logs.
observability.metrics: Runtime health, queue eligibility, posted/skipped/unresolved counts, authority state, and reconciliation state.
observability.alerts: Blocking runtime-health and scheduler outcomes must remain observable; automated alerting may be added later without changing this contract.

lesson_loop.standard_promotion_process: Operational findings are first corrected in XQueue, then generalized into TSAL only when reusable or sufficiently high-impact.
